subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call threshold data through workspace/internal hooks, and what payload/authority split should separate safe observation from typed plugin control?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but payload minimization, hook authority, event ordering, threshold configuration, and sensitive session/subagent/tool state exposure are public API and security-boundary choices that automation should not settle.

options.title: Observation-Only Internal Events
options.body: Add narrow workspace/internal lifecycle events with minimized metadata while leaving mutation, mid-turn control, and sensitive tool/session access in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Keep Lifecycle Plugin-Only
options.body: Treat existing typed plugin lifecycle hooks and related open PRs as the supported surface, and decline workspace hook expansion for this data.

options.title: Design Unified Lifecycle Contract First
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one lifecycle model covering internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, payloads, thresholds, permissions, and ordering.

recommendation.title: Observation-Only Internal Events
recommendation.body: Add narrow workspace/internal lifecycle events with minimized metadata while leaving mutation, mid-turn control, and sensitive tool/session access in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current history on the hook contract files and the current implementation boundary this decision would extend.
